subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: Regarding the City Council's concerns about traffic surrounding the proposed Smiling Faces daycare facility at 410 South Main Street: At 2hrs 52min into the video of the City Council meeting for 6/30/2020, your own City Engineers clearly illustrate the parking lot meets and exceeds the city's own codes for parking lot clearance. The comments from the City Councilman at 2:53:50 are slightly offensive and show that it has been some time, if any, since he has personally dropped off children at daycare. Smiling Faces runs a tight ship and there are NO "kids (are) getting out in the middle of the street and running across the road." ALL children enrolled at Smiling Faces are REQUIRED to be brought INSIDE and signed in by an adult, and the reverse upon checkout. It is quite rude for an elected or appointed city official to assume he cares more about my child's safety than myself. This same councilman expresses concern for the traffic on Main Street, when the current successfully operated daycare under the same management is on STATE Street. So a 25MPH mixed residential zone is now a greater threat than cutting across three to seven lanes of 45MPH+ traffic on a state route? A councilmember at 2:54:55 talks about turning left out of the parking lot, which again, I repeat - have you tried turning left out of any business along State Street? The parents and adults have managed just fine at the current facility for 3+ years. You may as well suggest all cars be banned from ever turning left onto any road for that argument to hold any weight. The few complaints you may have heard from one or two neighbors - people who actually live here - are likely a classic case of "not in my backyard." Orem claims to be Family City USA but a loud minority will scream and shout about the audacity of parents seeking childcare at their own expense so that we can go to the jobs those same residents insist we do to provide their services. Please also recall that the previous business here was a senior assisted living facility. The applicants are not bringing battering rams into an otherwise pristine cul-de-sac and demanding a steel mill be built. A similar business already operated here, caring for a vulnerable percentage of the population with loved ones who only wanted the best for them. Smiling Faces provides the best for our most vulnerable and precious population: our children. Please do not prevent or limit their ability to do so over some red tape. Jeff Lambson asking about traffic patterns impacted by Covid-19, but then walking back and stating 2015/2018 is not recent enough for a traffic study: which is it? Do you want current data based on extenuating circumstances, or reliable data based on historical use? This argument could be made once a week that "traffic patterns change." Yes, based on weather, global pandemics, seasons, construction, city development, whether there is a college football game that day, etc. That does not prevent businesses from operating. Comments continue at 3:12:30 regarding cars parked near the driveway. Again: have you, or will you be, "red-curbing" every single driveway that opens onto State Street or Main Street? You are unjustly making demands and requirements beyond those of our city code that have not been equally applied to other businesses. Taking away parking spots directly reduces their ability to run their business! "Losing students" is a loss of funding for the business owner, and a loss of childcare for your citizens! I am again baffled by the exchanges between Terry Peterson and Tom MacDonald at 3:15:30. "100 children running in and out between cars." Where are you getting these children from, gentlemen? Apparently you're under the impression that Orem parents just open their doors each morning and say "Good luck out there son, hope you don't get killed on the way to class!" Thank you to Mayor Brunst for being a voice of reason to point out that this is not the only childcare facility in our city, as well as the existing intersection at 400 South Main Street that has legal parking and has had legal parking for decades. David Spencer's comments at 3:46:25 are absurd and insulting, stating the city cannot manage weed abatement for an adjoining property and therefore will not be able to ensure rule compliance by the daycare facility. This insults his own employees as well as his voting constituents: if laws are written only with the expectation that they are only obeyed as long as they can be enforced, there would be none. Smiling Faces will follow the conditions Orem City sets for them because Orem City has set those conditions, period. Please show a little faith in your citizenry. The owners and managers at Smiling Faces have several degrees in education and have proven themselves as savvy and dedicated business people. Two public comments were read into the record from people that do not currently live in or near the neighborhood, as I do. One asked about a fence which the owners have stated they will voluntarily reinforce despite, again, already exceeding city requirements. For the third public comment expressing concern over the play area: Smiling Faces is already utilizing a space even smaller than this at their current location. They really are the best at what they do and consistently go above and beyond. In all, this expansion and relocation of Smiling Faces is actually a safer choice and provides better opportunities for their students than the current location. There is more parking, more space, and less overall traffic. Remember they are currently operating successfully on a busier road, with fewer parking spots, which they share with a trailer park and a restaurant. If anything, Smiling Faces has proven they can make the best of any situation and meet a high standard set in less than fantastic conditions. They should not be punished for wanting to give their clients better services. Please reconsider the conditions placed upon this small locally-owned and reliable business while remembering our claim that Orem is the best place to raise a family. Please let me raise my family here; stop making it harder than it needs to be. Your Planning Commission voted unanimously for approval. Trust your staff and your own appointed Board members to do the jobs you assigned them to do. And just to be clear, this "Hispanic" business (as referred to by your own council during the meeting) does not only serve the "Hispanic" community. I can't believe I even have to say this, but it is serving the OREM Community. And I am not of Latinx or Spanish-speaking origin. Please do the right thing and approve this conditional use -which you can still revoke later, if needed! - during your next meeting on July 14th. Put the same faith in us that we put in you when we vote.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: Hello, I am writing as somebody who has formerly owned a child care business. I understand that German and Luz Pardo are looking to expand their child care center; and I understand that this expansion depends upon them acquiring a parcel of land to do so. Child care, in Utah, has always been in high demand. Especially now, with so much uncertainty as to the upcoming school year, there is going to be a high demand for child care. There has always been a high demand for child care in Utah; in fact, a substantial proportion of Utah child care providers are not licensed, and therefore not subject to the training and inspection of licensed providers. But often, waiting lists in licensed facilities are too long, and parents have no other choice but to put their children in an unlicensed private home, often with only one adult, therefore, nobody to supervise the methods of that one adult. Therefore, parents are taking a risk by trusting an unlicensed provider. However, the demand for childcare is so high, that sometimes, it’s all a parent can do. Therefore, it seems to me that, when experienced child care professionals come to you with a plan to expand, I would I hope you would not dismiss their request out right. I understand that these professionals have completed engineering reports with regard to the property, I also understand that the bank is withholding authorization of the loan pending the approval of the Orem city Council. I understand that two of the council members are concerned, but their concerns were rather nonspecific. Surely, these council members would trust the word of bonded engineers? I also understand that this particular daycare presents unique opportunities for the children who attend. The opportunity to learn a second language at such a young age can help a child immensely in their learning journey. Bilingualism is not only a valuable job skill, but studies have shown that children who learn a second language early on, actually speak as a native speaker. There are also studies to show that children who learn two or more languages from an early age, have better performance in school and higher IQs. Beyond that, in the western hemisphere, Spanish is the dominant language, and those who speak only English are at a substantial disadvantage as Latin American economies are emerging. And, like I was saying earlier, the younger child learns a second language, the more pure and true is their syntax and vocabulary, which when used to communicate, builds trust with native Spanish speakers. In my daycare, I taught my children American sign language and Spanish, along with English. My clients were very happy that their children had those opportunities. As my daughter entered grade school, I returned to the workforce outside my home, but one thing I made sure to do, is to put her in a school that valued a diversity of cultures and languages. The district my daughter attended had students from more than 100 different countries and spoke more than 100 different languages. My daughter now has lifelong friends, people who are from all over the globe. That type of education cannot be taught in a more homogenous school. And the value of that education is immense, since we now live within a global economy. In the modern world, it’s children who have learned to navigate many different world cultures who will have the advantage ove children who are more sheltered. In the past, so many business people have lost accounts or severed relationships with international vendors and clients because they are culturally clumsy. It seems to me, that the unique opportunity presented by this multicultural daycare center would give the children of Orem the opportunity to practice global cultural awareness. At any rate, as our businesses begin to open up as we emerge from the pandemic, and since full- time public schooling is not a given at this point, and indeed, I can see children attending school only part time until Utah‘s surge of cases is under control, the one thing parents are going to need most, in order to go back to work, is quality childcare. A final word about the goals of German and Luz Pardo’s expansion. I understand that they are expanding in order to accommodate siblings in the same daycare. As a former daycare provider, I cannot tell you how valuable it is to keep siblings together in child care. Modern-day kids live a lonely enough life, and with parents working full-time, young children often go without seeing their families For 10 hours a day. If German and Luz Pardo can allow siblings to go to the same daycare, it provides immense comfort to the little ones and strengthens family bonds. Please consider expediting their application, so they can get their expansion underway for the upcoming school year.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: I am deeply concerned and disappointed that you voted "nay" or "present" on the conditional use permit for Smiling Faces Bilingual Center at 410 North Main Street. I watched the entire recording of the City Council meeting on June 30, 2020 and frankly was appalled at the ending. It is clear that German Pardo (the applicant) has followed everything required, has met all ordinances and conditions, and therefore the council has no administrative right to decline this permit. The condition added by Mayor Brunst for redlining seemed reasonable, though not necessary, to any potential meet the visibility issues. Though I would argue, based on the evidence I present, that the northern most stall on Main Street does NOT need to be redlined (in other words, that parking stall should remain, and redlining should not reduce that parking stall). I was also concerned that there seemed to be repeated remarks about taking out the 5 parking stalls on the south side of the parking lot. After the engineer and planning commission representative clearly stated, there is no problem with this. There was even a diagram showing a large truck making a 3-point turn without using any of the space. I was curious to know just how tight this was, so I drove to the property. Please see my attached videos for the many turnarounds and parking situations. It seems this was a nefarious move to get the facility to house fewer children. To address the concern about 100's of kids being dropped off at the same time and the safety concern. It is clear by this repeated statement that you have no experience dropping a child off at a daycare facility that requires you to physically walk your child in. Smiling Faces is currently in a much worse situation parking wise and has had zero problems. As someone who has dropped off and picked up a child at their current location, I have never had trouble getting a parking spot and I have never been at the door waiting for my child with more than 2 parents at any time. And my pickup time is at 5:30. And I have never been in danger of someone hitting me or my child. This is because of the high safety expectations that Smiling Faces has required for their business. I previously emailed the public comment praising Smiling Faces for doing amazing with the less than ideal conditions of crossing three lanes of heavy state traffic, with cars parked on a street with low visibility. This is not an elementary school where the "tuck and roll" drop off method is used and there are 3x the amount of kids at all the same time. 100 children is the max, with multiple children presumably in the same car. This is an organized facility, with staggered drop off and pick up schedules, and adults who are licensed drivers safely driving through (This was presented as evidence in the traffic study). In addition, the Orem City Code 22-6-9. Regulations Governing Particular Uses specifies in Section G-1 That Commercial Daycares be located on collector or arterial streets makes this seem like your argument could never be satisfied as arterial streets are going to have considerably more traffic than others. Again, Smiling Faces REQUIRES the child's guardian to physically walk them in, sign the book, and drop them off (or pick up). This expansion is to allow siblings to be at the same facility and to open it up for infants. Orem is in DESPERATE need of childcare. It is the only way businesses will grow and the community will be served. Smiling Faces is the ONLY daycare I found in Orem to have ZERO infractions on their license. Another testament to their priority on safety. Another concern brought up in the video was about public notice and neighborhoods notice. The public notice was posted, 130 notices were mailed, it was posted on the Orem website, the hotline, and the state website as per the Planning Commission notification. I am also attaching a picture of that public notice. Clearly, they were notified. And as Jason Bench described, the Wyoming and American Fork resident complaints of not receiving notification has nothing to do with the administrative proceedings for a Conditional Use Permit (see my attached letter) Please also read my attached letter concerning the legal/administrative matter of your rejection. It is against State Municipal Code to reject a conditional use permit if the conditions can reasonably be met and mitigate the perceived detriments. PUBLIC COMMENT is NOT allowed for decision making unless is it for factual evidence. Just because a neighbor (or the family of a neighbor living in Wyoming) wasn't notified does not have any bearing on the decision for a conditional use permit, or if the neighbor just doesn't want it. See Utah Code in my attached letter for further explanation. Plentiful expert opinion from the multiple engineers, the city planner, and the planning commission, that the applicant is complying with the conditions put forth and meets all city ordinances and provided substantial evidence as such for the record. Council members cannot capriciously decide not to approve it, there must be recorded evidence for the rejection and there is none. Where is the evidence for rejecting it? There was no evidence given that the applicant is not capable of meeting the conditions put forth. And as far as I am concerned, there isn't any that could bar Smiling Faces from receiving the permit. https://propertyrights.utah.gov/conditional-uses/ Because public comment is only allowed to produce factual evidence (see Utah Code on my attachment), I present this google drive folder that contains video of the intersection taken on Saturday, July 11, 2020 at around 6:15pm. I took the videos with an iPhone where there were two vehicles present in the eastern most car stall on 400 South (a Honda minivan), and the northern most stall on Main street (a Toyota Rav 4). These stalls seemed to draw concern, deemed as the two likely stalls to cause visibility and traffic problems. These videos show that drivers clearly do not need to go into the "middle of the intersection" as one council member proclaimed on the June 30 meeting, the drivers have fine visibility, even with a setting sun, and drivers can turn left onto main street even with a car in the northern most stall as well as a car occupying the left turn lane on main street. I hate to think that this may be a "not in my backyard" racist issue, or that someone on the council would personally profit off of rejecting the permit. I have no direct evidence of this and do not want to make any unbecoming accusations, but it's hard to ignore the observations. Hispanic owners of a daycare adjacent to a mobile home park, serving both white and hispanic (and possibly other races and ethnicities, I don't know) members of the community, wanting to expand near affluent homes. And based on my drive around the neighborhood it is predominantly white. This makes it hard not to draw conclusions or raise an eyebrow at what the motivation for a capricious rejection would be, given that such a rejection is against code and not within the administrative right of the Orem City Council. Please see my attached material. It is imperative that you do the right thing, support local businesses, support the community, and do your job in approving this reasonable conditional use permit for Smiling Faces to expand this critical need business. Again, this is not whether you like it or not. Your administrative duty is to approve that the applicant has met all conditions laid out and are in compliance with laws and city ordinances. This is regardless of your personal feelings. I expect to see a unanimous vote on Tuesday in the council meeting as it should have been done on June 30, 2020. I also wonder if anything but an immediate unanimous vote could happen as that should have been the case on June 30. If this goes to appeal (if you vote no again) and involves the courts, based on advice from legal counsel the City is 100% in the wrong here, specifically you, who voted with a capricious no. Background: I was born and raised in Orem, Utah in which I have taught at Timpanogos High School and went on to earn my PhD at BYU as a research scientist. I have lived in Orem most of my life and have settled my family (my husband and 3 children) in a North Orem neighborhood. I have had 2 children attend Smiling Faces (1 currently) for the past year. My entire family is white (not that it should matter but because of my concerns of the racial discrimination aspect to this situation I think it could be important information) She also provided Pictures in Shared Drive and Copy of ULCT CUP Handbook (too much to attach)

comment: I comment here as an Orem resident who has two children who have attended Smiling Faces Daycare for over two years. In addition, my family and I permanently reside near the area under consideration near 400 South, just a little further west. I really hope I am not too late in having another voice heard on this. Having listened to the meeting that took place on June 30th, it appeared to me that you had city planners, engineers, zoning and other city officers on the call who had basically signed off on everything and were essentially just waiting for the blessing of the council. I almost wonder what the point of having the council members voice their personal opinions and concerns at all on this was when it was already determined that the proper permits, research, safety, and planning had already been completed and signed off. But I will admit that this is the first council meeting I have ever listened to or reviewed the minutes for. So, this might be standard. At any rate, I'd like to comment on the concerns that were presented in the meeting. #1. As I mentioned, we have two children, a now four and six year old, who have been attending Smiling Faces for over two years and I can say for a fact that for over two years every single day I have personally walked my kids to and from the front office of the school and had to personally sign off in a detailed log they kept on the exact time that we arrived/departed (both as per the standards/policies set by the school). Not only that, we were ALWAYS greeted by one of the staff within seconds of arriving on the front steps. The image procured during the meeting of a hundred kids running around wildly in and out of the street or parking lot couldn't be further off base. Taking my kids to daycare is exactly like me taking my kids to literally any other establishment and this is further helped by the policies they've established to make the drop off/pickup as seamless and safe as possible. It has never taken longer than 2-3 minutes to drop off or pick up my children and I've always had plenty of parking spots to choose from at the current location (despite that being far less options than the proposed new location). We've lived off of 400 South for the better part of a year and a half. I drive the 400 South road from 800 West to State Street multiple times a day (to the daycare, restaurants, mall, grocery, errands, etc.). I can tell you that the intersection of main street and 400 South is not busy AT ALL. It wouldn't matter if you did a traffic study yesterday, 6 months ago or 6 years ago. It just does not get anywhere near the same amount of traffic that Orem Boulevard or State Street gets. As for the parking space allotment, it appeared from the meeting that that concern was resolved (I hope). As I said, the daycare already currently shares about 11 other spaces with several other surrounding locations and I've never had an issue finding a parking space. Having 26 spaces at the new location, or even a few less than that as per any of the adjustments that were suggested would be more than enough. As for the blind turning onto main street let's be honest...what street in Orem ISN'T a blind turn. People already park way too close to intersections/stop signs and I don't think it would be fair to make that a deal breaker in this situation when literally everywhere else I go in this city I experience the same thing. The biggest thing I think I can really comment on here is what this business means to me in my life. This is the best daycare I've ever run across hands down. My kids come home each day with a stack of crafts, art, activities, projects, and all kinds of stories about all the cool things they learned about/did that day. If you look at the pictures of 'space day' or 'camping day' or 'shopping day' or any of the other days you can really see how all out they go with everything. I'd encourage you to read the reviews and peruse their facebook posts to observe the pictures of the kids really just loving life and getting the most out of a school experience. I don't speak Spanish myself, but my kids are learning it at the same time as experiencing all of this awesome stuff. Let's encourage dedicated small local business owners like Herman and Luz in pursuit of their dreams of providing an awesome bilingual program by approving this measure. Thank you!

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: I am a resident of Orem with no children therefore no need for a daycare or to know about the daycare facilities within our city, however within the span of 5 minutes I was able to understand not only the need for the expansion of Smiling Faces Bilingual Childcare Center but also the thorough, thoughtful and immense planning that German Pardo has taken to ensure this new building is the safest and has every child in mind. The facility has a specific policy in place that requires all children be walked into the building with an adult to be sign in/out meaning the adult doing the drop off must park and escort the child inside/outside. There are no safety factors regarding "100 child running out willy nilly". In addition, parents sign up for a schedule to stagger pick up/drop off times which allows for a few amount of children coming and going at one time. The concerns proposed by the council regarding child safety surround the public street and parking lot were addressed several times and factually dispelled, however they continued to be a point of discussion. Why? The planning commission and engineers for the building have reiterated that there is NO LEGAL reason to deny this permit and have agreed it is a safe place to put a daycare. I was extremely disappointed to hear about the behavior exhibited by Jeff Lambson, Tom MacDonald, Terry Peterson, David Spencer and Brent Sumner. The comments from the first council meeting regarding this daycare showed a willful ignorance to the information being presented as all safety and legal measures are being met and a tone of prejudice by attempting to grasp for any reason to dismantle and discredit the work German and the engineers have done to ensure the permit is not approved. subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: Dear Mayor and City Council Members, I have lived in Orem City for all of my life and love this community. Orem truly does things differently than most other communities that struggle with being fair. I am writing to the Orem City Council to strongly ask that they approve Smiling Faces Day Care without tying their hands any more than has already been done. subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: My name is Brenda Eyring and I am a former user of the Smiling Faces daycare on 400 E in Orem, near Sharon Elementary School. We live in that neighborhood and my then 7-year-old daughter attended their daycare before and after school. I appreciated their services and I loved that they were located so close to our home and our school. I was impressed with their professionalism and organization. Paperwork was always organized, the children encountered predictable routine, the premises were always neat and tidy, etc. They were a real asset to our neighborhood, and we were grateful for their services at that time. subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: My husband and I were residents of Orem 20 years. I am a former member of the Orem City Planning Commission and the Orem City Council. I am also a commercial real estate agent, but I am not personally involved in the sale or leasing of the subject property and have no relationship with Smiling Faces Daycare. I do not work at the same company as the real estate agent representing the property and have no personal or financial interes t in this property. I am writing as a citizen who is concerned about the City Council discussions and actions taken at the City Council’s last hearing on this item on June 30th. Before going into the specifics on these topics, however, I want to review the rules of Conditional Use Permits. Utah State Code, section 10-9a-507, states: (2)(a)(i) A land use authority shall approve a conditional use if reasonable conditions are proposed, or can be imposed, to mitigate the reasonably anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed use in accordance with applicable standards. (ii) The requirement described in Subsection (2)(a)(i) to reasonably mitigate anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed conditional use does not require elimination of the detrimental effects. The Office of the Property Rights Ombudsman for the State of Utah explains that “Conditions may be imposed to mitigate, or lessen, the detrimental effects of the proposed use. The conditions must be reasonable, must address the identified effects, and must refer to the applicable standards already identified in the land use ordinance.” At both the Work-session pre-meeting and during the City Council Meeting on June 30th, City Attorney Steve Earl, read this section of the Utah State Code to the Council as a point of reference for how the Council should consider the application, and what their powers and obligations are in this legislative action. The question, it seems, is whether the applicant can “reasonably mitigate anticipated detrimental effects.” From viewing the video of the Council’s Zoom meeting, it appeared that the primary concerns about “detrimental effects” were safety of the children as they arrive at the daycare and leave the daycare, and parking inside the existing parking lot and along the street adjacent to the property on the North and East sides. When the Planning Commission forwarded a unanimous recommendation for approval of the Conditional Use Permit, they stipulated the following conditions: 1. That all visitors, employees and other persons who arrive at the facility in connection with the Commercial Day Care facility be legally parked on the on - site parking lot or on that part of the street immediately abutting the site. 2. That signage be provided on the on-site parking lot that clearly indicates pick-up/drop-off stalls. 3. That one stall in the parking lot be used as a vehicle back-up area. 4. That the facility be limited to a maximum occupancy of one hundred (100) children for both buildings combined. 5. That two ADA stalls be provided in the parking lot. 6. That all chi ldren must be picked up and dropped off within the existing parking lot. That no more than ten (10) pick up/drop off vehicles shall be allowed within any ten (10) minute period. 7. That no more than ten (10) pick up/drop off vehicles shall be allowed within any ten (10) minute period. Applicant has agreed to comply with these conditions to assure the safety of the children and to mitigate the possible “detrimental effects” of the drop-off and pick-up. Applicant demonstrated that they have scheduled times for parents to drop-off children, and that all children must be walked into the building by an adult and signed in upon arrival. When picking children up from Daycare, parents are required to park and go inside the building to sign their children out and then walk them to their vehicle. Council Member Peterson, in his discussion of potential “detrimental effects” said – I’m paraphrasing – “Parents don’t follow rules” and “children run around.” I interpreted this to mean that he felt the proposed conditions would not mitigate the possible “detrimental effects.” State Law specifically states that reasonable mitigation does not require the elimination of the detrimental effects. Parents may very well choose to disobey rules, but if they do, it is the parent putting children at risk, and this could happen at any legally operating business in the city. It could happen at City Parks, at the Scera Pool, at the grocery store. I submit that Utah Law does not give the City Council power to deny a Conditional Use Permit based on the fear of what a parent may do. It is merely incumbent upon the City Council to apply reasonable conditions so that the business can establish operating procedures to meet these conditions. I am convinced that the Applicant has demonstrated their capacity and willingness to do so. Council Member Sumner repeatedly requested that the Applicant consider removing the 5 parking stalls in front of the South building to increase vehicular capacity to turn around to exit the parking lot. Both City Attorney Earl and Traffic Engineer Sam Kelly pointed out that the existing parking lot is a legal parking lot. In other words, as it is currently constructed, it meets the legal requirements of a parking lot and is in compliance with Orem City’s Development Code which has specific requirements for the size of parking stalls and the distance between parking rows. Because the Daycare drop -off and pick-up model requires parents to park their car and come inside the building, removing parking stalls to accommodate the perceived need for additional turn-around space would severely limit the number of parents that can be legally parked to accomplish the drop -off and pick-up. Additionally, removing stalls would be requiring the Applicant to construct a parking lot configuration for their business that exceeds the legal requirements for a parking lot. Utah State Law specifically states that conditions must be reasonable, and must refer to the applicable standards already identified in the land use ordinance. I believe the request to eliminate legal parking stalls, both in the existing parking lot and along 400 South and Main Street, violates the requirement in Utah State Law that the conditions must be “reasonable” and “must refer to the applicable standards already identified in the land use ordinance.” Finally, Council Member Spencer suggested that the City restrict parking on 400 South and Main Street – parking that is currently legal on-street parking. He also stated that he didn’t think [the use] was safe and just didn’t like it. Regarding on-street parking, again referring to the Utah State Code, the current on-street parking is legal under the ordinances of Orem City. This business’s ability to use these parking spaces should be assured by the applicable standards alr eady identified in Orem’s Land Use Ordinance. Any other business that was a permitted use in this property (ie: Residential Treatment Center for Youth, Therapeutic School, Assisted Living, Sober Living Home, or a Residential Facility for Disabled Persons) would not be asked to remove legal parking spaces because they are not subject to “conditions” for their approved use. I believe the conditions recommended by Staff and forwarded to the City Council by the Planning Commission with a unanimous recommendation for approval address to the extent possible “reasonable conditions” to assure the safety of the children and the neighborhood. Throughout Orem, we have many places where there are vehicles and children – Public Schools, parks, the City Center Baseball Fields, the Library, the SCERA park pool. When using these facilities, we should all exercise care – even if there aren’t designated parking spots for dropping our kids off, and even if we don’t have a drop -off schedule to abide by. This business has agreed to take these extra measures to assure safety and to comply with conditions to obtain their Conditional Use Permit. I encourage you to approve the Applicant’s Conditional Use Permit with reasonable conditions as directed by Utah State Law and in conformance with the legal standards already outlined in the Orem City Municipal Code.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: I grew up in Orem, just down the street from the location that Smiling Faces Daycare is trying to occupy. I have talked to members of the neighborhood and they have no problem with the daycare being there. I have also read comments and watched video of council meeting. Zoning for that area allows for a daycare. 13 requirements have been met, including a costly parking study. Parking is more than sufficient for the daycare requirements, children are not left to run through the parking lot, and there are staggered drop offs. I have used daycare services before, and it does not take 15 minutes to drop off or pick up a child, that is a very generous time slot. As I listened to comments from the council, it felt like the council was trying to find reasons for not allowing the business. I have parked in thousands of parking lots, and not had an issue with backing out of a parking space that has the same amount of space. That seems like a reach. Also, a Daycare/preschool is very different from an elementary school drop off, parents have to walk the children into the building, they don't let them loose. I guarantee that there is plenty of time in a day for 100 cars to go through that area and I doubt they will be filled to capacity every single day. People also carpool for preschool which are the busiest . The opinion of some of these council members are very narrow. It is disappointing. As far as having a daycare in the neighborhood, there is nothing more beautiful than the sound of children playing. As far as safety, there is very little deviant behavior (if any) that comes from a daycare, and would not be much different from a senior living center. I feel that the presenters proved the safety concerns were taken care of. As far as the play area, fences are easy to build. You do not need a lot of space for kids to play outside and times are staggered again. Daycares have indoor play space. Neighbors, only two commented, and to be honest, zoning allows for this. Meetings were noticed, sometimes neighbors just don't pay attention. Not a valid complaint. You have to have a legitimate reason to deny. I am sure the neighborhood would rather have a daycare than a drug treatment center. There have been no complaints about this facility. They are well respected in the community. It fills a need within the community. I am disappointed in the comments about this being a "hispanic business". The planning commission has already approved the plan (with all the traffic "concerns"). I encourage you to approve this permit. Make Orem a better place by allowing this business to function and add to the community. Don't give Orem a black eye by not supporting small businesses and people doing their best to improve the community. They are hardworking people that have bent over backward trying to meet the requirements. This business would be an asset and it is a needed business. They have met all the requirements, approve the permit. Legally, you need to do that. I will reserve my personal opinion, but I am concerned about the reasons that some council members are being difficult on this decision. It is disappointing.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: I am writing to share how essential Smiling Faces is to the Orem community and what an asset it would be for Orem should the proposed location on 400 South and Main Street be approved. I am an adjunct professor at Brigham Young University, and my husband works full time as a marketer. We have lived in Utah County the last 12 years. We have had our two children enrolled in care at Smiling Faces for 3 years now. We have utilized childcare services from 3 other businesses, until we found Smiling Faces and found it superior in every way: the safety precautions they take, the curriculum they practice, and the love they give to the families they serve is unmatched. My children have grown immensely since being enrolled at Smiling Faces: intellectually, emotionally, and socially. Smiling Faces is helping my children become citizens that Orem would be proud of, citizens that respect, honor, and care for each other. During a time when people are calling for equality and diversity in business, I am grateful for the opportunity to choose Smiling Faces, because my sons are learning it doesn’t matter the color of your skin; everyone deserves love and opportunity. Childcare is hard enough to find, without the extra difficulties COVID-19 has added to parents’ troubles in finding not just adequate care for their children, but care they are happy about, care they know matches the care they give to their children in their own homes. We found it particularly difficult to find a childcare facility that offers part time care, and we previously paid full-time fees for part time service, at another Orem facility that had a worse parking situation than the more than adequate parking at the proposed site of 400 South and Main Street. We settled for a less than desirable situation so our family could have our basic childcare needs met. No parent should be in that situation. Smiling Faces was literally our solution and saving grace, and it is that same answer for so many other families and could be that answer for many more if Smiling Faces is allowed to move to the proposed location. If the council denies Smiling Faces the opportunity to grow their business, they are denying their community the opportunity to grow, removing the possibility of work for many families. In regard to some of the concerns brought up in the previous council meeting; I would like to share my experience. I drop off and pick up my children from Smiling Faces Monday through Friday. I make numerous left-hand turns (and right hand turns for that matter) from the moment I leave my home. Many of them have reduced visibility due to parked cars, large fences, greenery, other homes, etc. But they are legal—just as the intersection and driveway at the proposed site is legal. Are you willing to revoke business privileges wherever there is a turn with less than ideal visibility? If so, you would be stunting Orem immensely, needing to close nearly every business that finds itself on the corner of an intersection. Regarding the concern of crowds and crowds of children and families all arriving at the same time, causing a backup in traffic: Again, during the 700+ times I have dropped off or picked up my children during the last three years, I have never seen 100 children in 100 cars piled up on state street, all trying to enter Smiling Faces at once. In the mornings, it is rare when I see another parent dropping off their child. During the afternoon pickup, I see one, maybe two other parents for a total of 3 families at once. Smiling Faces runs a tight ship, their protocols are well- thought-out and executed because they know that’s what it takes to keep the children they care for safe. If you could see the way Smiling Faces is handling the current pandemic, guiding children through temperature checks, hand washing/sanitizing, providing facemasks for all children (and getting them to actually wear them), there would be no doubt in your mind that this is a company that exceeds expectations and requirements and serves their community in every possible way. I am baffled that the council seems more concerned with comments coming from a person currently residing in Wyoming and a person currently residing in American Fork than they are for concerns raised by persons in the community the council actually represents, like my family and Orem business. Are you willing to put the desires of the small number of homes surrounding the property above the actual needs of so many more families? Please reconsider, take these facts into account when making your decision tonight and approve the request Smiling Faces has made.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: My husband and I have lived in Orem over 40 years & have raised our children here. We are now assisting raising some grandchildren who have been attending Smiling Faces. Here are our observations: 1. The facilities are spotless & the staff is wonderful with the children. 2. The drop off/pick up policy prevents any children from “running around unattended” in the parking lot. You have to go in & sign the children in & out. Every time. They have staggered the times so well that I have never encountered more than 2 other parents picking up or dropping off. The current parking situation is tight (but they have made it work with the staggered times) and I hate trying to get back out on State Street especially with other cars parked on the sides of the roads. The proposed location has a slower speed limit & much less traffic. 3. Any question of excess neighborhood traffic is ridiculous. We had a halfway house put in near our neighborhood a few years ago & the neighbors displeasure at possible increased traffic had no bearing on them getting the permit. The visibility coming out of the proposed location is fine- I checked it out myself. 4. It is evident that the owners have made every effort to comply with the laws and requirements. Why are they being made to jump through hoops that hint at discrimination? Is it because this is an affluent area? Or the fact that they are minority owned? There is a great need in Orem for quality licensed day care and this business has a proven track record. We should be helping them expand not hindering them. The fact that they incorporate bilingual teaching is such a plus. We need to be encouraging great minority owned business not trying to eliminate them. 5. The difficulty you are putting them through makes me wonder if there is some hidden agenda present. Or at least as I stated before possible discrimination. I certainly hope that is not the case. Orem is better than that. Natalie and Bryan Laird I would like to respectfully ask you to reconsider your current stand on the issue regarding a new location for Smiling Faces Daycare. My son has been attending Smiling Faces for about 2.5 yrs. I can say with 100% certainty, they have boosted his knowledge and fostered his intelligence more than I would've thought or expected. He loves going to school everyday and is excited to see his teachers and friends. Even after moving 20 min south of Orem due to buying a house, we have decided to keep our son (4) at Smiling Faces because of the incredible impact Luz and her employees have had in our lives. Luz and German Pardo have always handled business with honesty and integrity, which as working parents, is immensely appreciated. They teach the kids everything from basics like the alphabet to important current social climate issues. They're an incredible asset to not only the community of Orem but to the future of Utah, for our kids are the future of the world. In conclusion, this expansion and relocation of Smiling Faces is a much safer choice and provides better opportunities for their students than the current location. There is more parking, more space, and less overall traffic. Remember they are currently operating successfully on a busier road, with fewer parking spots, which they share with a trailer park and a restaurant. If anything, Smiling Faces has proven they can make the best of any situation and meet a high standard set in less than fantastic conditions. They should not be punished for wanting to give their clients better services. Please reconsider the conditions placed upon this small locally-owned and reliable business while remembering our claim that Orem is the best place to raise a family.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: I would like to voice a concern I have raised through things that I have been made aware of recently. I know that public comment without factual evidence has no bearing on approving a Conditional Use Permit. And while my comment now is connected with my previous letter, this is not necessarily to be used in determining the CUP. My comment now is to raise public concern about the intention and underlying principles of the City Council in making decisions for the city. I recently had a conversation about the neighbors surrounding the proposed new Smiling Faces Bilingual Center. It turns out that conversations questioning the owners citizenship status happened when the owners were introducing themselves to the neighborhood. Why would that even come up in a conversation when owners are introducing themselves and trying to be "good neighbors" as the city ordinance requires (and is just common decency)? When I have introduced myself to new people, not once have I been asked if I was a citizen of the United States. Given that "public outcry" from the neighbors is likely why Councilmen Lambson, Sumner, Spencer, Peterson, and MacDonald rejected the CUP is deeply concerning. Those Councilmembers should rethink who and what they are supporting in our city. I will not tolerate racist sentiments from my city leaders. I have higher expectations of our great community than to accept that these types of conversations are appropriate. Thank you for your time. I appreciate this great city and the opportunity I have had to continue living here and raise my family.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: I live directly south of the proposed daycare center at 468 South Main St. I am grateful for the opportunity here to share some concerns.My largest concern is with the increased traffic that the daycare would bring - both the safety and inconvenience of this traffic. Although the cars parked on the two roads are legally allowed, visibility is very poor when there are cars parked in these areas. The intersection just east of 400th south and Main has gotten busier and busier with UVU, Midtown, State Street, Orem Elementary, and Noah Webster, and will just get busier. With 100 kids being dropped off and picked up daily, I can only imagine that cars would end up backed up into and through that (Orem Boulevard) intersection, as well as down 400th south and Main Street which are both single-lane roads. I imagine this will be happening at its worst between the hours of 8 and 9:30 am, which is the time I need to be backing out of my own driveway on Main Street to head to work myself. After backing out of my driveway, I would then have to wait in the line of daycare dropoff cars going north on Main Street before I could get out onto 400th South and State Street. Where this is a residential district, having this traffic every single day would greatly diminish the quality of life of those living in close proximity to the daycare on Main Street. Lines of waiting cars in the street with engines running is a safety concern, a health hazard for us and our neighbors, and an unpleasant residential experience.I understand that there may be a need for a daycare in Orem City, however, it is obvious to me that a business of this size is not suited to this property. There are no other businesses near this size along the entire length of Main Street or 400th South. This is a residential area that should be preserved as such.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: I would like to add my support to the approval of the conditional use permit for Smiling Faces Daycare. I am the parent of two young children living in Orem, and finding childcare is so tough! Smiling Faces has proposed great measures to keep kids safe on the property. By the planning commission's review, it seems parking and traffic control is adequate. Please support great childcare businesses like Smiling Faces in thriving in Orem so that families have adequate choices when finding care for their kids! Also, latinx business owners provide critical services to all of Orem, not just fellow latinx residents. Thank you

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: I know the board is considering a request of the Smiling Faces Child Care Center to move into a new bigger building. I use to work for Workforce Services who does licensing for child care in Utah. Orem always had a shortage of good child care centers. This center has been in Orem for awhile and is highly recommended. I feel it would be in the best interest of the council to approve this request. The city needs the increase in capacity that this move would allow. Currently I don’t have a need for childcare, but my children do, they have had a hard time finding good options for childcare in Utah county. This new location will give citizens more options and will allow for more children to be cared for by licensed providers.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: I live just south of the proposed daycare. I travel on 400 South and Main Street regularly, including commute to work (pandemic permitting). I’ll keep my comments brief but in sum I am opposed to the daycare in this location. Here are my concerns:- The location in question is not well suited for that amount of traffic. Two weeks ago when this was discussed the phrase “10 cars in 10 minutes” was thrown around and considering the fact that each car needs to park and walk their children into the building, along with the size of the parking lot leads me to believe that it will take much more than one minute per car to enter and exit that small parking area. - The length of time it will take for a car to pull in, park, unload children (sometimes several), pull out (at least a 3-point turn, if not more) and exit the parking lot will cause backups that extend into both Main Street and 400 South. - The left turn lane on Main Street to turn west onto 400 S makes the lanes even narrower, further congesting the intersection. Also the addition of the employee parking on both streets will make for very narrow lanes and higher chances of accidents. - This is a residential neighborhood with multiple driveways surrounding the facility. I can’t imagine what it would be like for my family and neighbors to have to wait for extended amounts of time to enter or exit their homes.I have spoken personally to both husband and wife of looking to start the daycare and they are very nice people. I do not have a bad word to say about them or their business and I hope they are able to expand as they hope- Orem needs more daycares, especially run by people of every race. That would create a stronger and more diverse community. But I also hope to have the residential experience that we expect by living in this wonderful neighborhood. I do not think having a daycare in this location will provide us with such.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: Let smiling faces daycare open! They have done and passed every task you made them do. You are discriminating against them for no reason. Orem needs to do better

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: Over the course of the Planning Commission meeting and two City Council meetings, multiple people have mentioned that Orem needs more daycare and that this business is well-managed and a valued contributor to the Orem community. I’m not questioning those assertions but they are not pertinent to this issue. The issue is whether this location can support the business at its requested client capacity without affecting the safety of the neighbors, daycare clients, and pass- thru traffic. Nothing I’ve observed during this two week continuation period changes the parking, traffic, and safety concerns previously expressed to the Council. These concerns are based on 30 years of experience living in my current home (411 South 60 West) directly west of the property. In short, this is an increasingly traveled and congested area with poor visibility that has already been negatively impacted by the Midtown Village development and overall traffic increases; adding parking and traffic from a business that marginally meets the requirements only escalates the safety hazards in the area. I ask you not to ignore these safety concerns voiced from the experience of multiple longtime neighbors by shoehorning this business into this location.
